proof.criterion: INFRA-528 cleanup and round-5 flake fix
proof.surface: Dispatch unit suite; Firefox comment-thread rows
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src e2e/__tests__; bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts --project firefox --workers=1 --repeat-each 10 -g "a comment holding|a reply to a comment|renderer refuses|label holding markup|another language stays code|in a comment runs nothing"
proof.observed: 2612 unit tests pass; 60/60 Firefox comment-thread runs pass.
proof.negativeControl: Timer started at queue time: the ready-delay case fails with 'it did not finish within 0.05 seconds'; open-fence pop removed: the callout case fails (length 2, expected 1); worker setter removed: the comment row shows 'Cannot set property self of #<DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope> which has only a getter'

trickyParts: The editor view sets a mermaid block's layout only in ProseMirror's update; an answer only fills the shadow root and the status, so a late drawing never moves the contentDOM (a unit test watches with a MutationObserver; moving it on answer hangs the happy-dom run).
Every engine Playwright runs (and Safari 27) anchors the scroll natively, so R7/R8 turn overflow-anchor off to prove the page's own re-run; without that the rows pass with the re-run removed.

The focus runs again only when a diagram is still waiting (mermaidDrawsWaiting), so a document with no pending diagram pulses its target once. An earlier version focused twice; VersionView.test.tsx then failed and bun's failure diff of the fake editor grew past 3 GB, which OOM-killed the pod several times.
deviations: Plan v2 (dispatch://INFRA-532/artifact/plan-md) supersedes plan.json: documents draw in the worker by the INFRA-138 architect's decision.
R7 and R8 fail at the red commit (they assert no diagram is drawn before the release), as the architect requires every new row to fail before the change; the plan's table said they pass.

R6 routes the worker bundle to a stub that never answers (INFRA-713's approach, the architect's instruction); the INFRA-528 comment too-large row keeps main's text except its openCommentThread lead, and is left to INFRA-713 and CI.
Browser runs are one project at a time with --workers=1 (pod memory); the full four-project run is CI's.
The comment too-large row was not run in the pod at the head: it draws 800 nodes for real.
